title: Invariant Preservation and Complexity Analysis of a C++ HyperLogLog Cardinality Estimation Algorithm

abstract: HyperLogLog (HLL) is a probabilistic data structure that estimates the cardinality of large multisets with sub-linear memory. This work presents a rigorously engineered C++ implementation that preserves key invariants of the HLL register array while achieving the theoretical $O(\log m)$ update complexity of a balanced search structure. We formalize the rank-update invariant, prove its monotonicity, and demonstrate that the estimator remains unbiased under the standard hash-mixing assumptions. Static analysis of the source yields a succinct abstract syntax tree with 146 lines of code and a single function block, confirming the absence of hidden recursion or dynamic allocation. The algorithm's asymptotic bounds are $O(1)$ per insertion and $O(1)$ for cardinality estimation, with a space requirement of $m = 2^p$ registers. The implementation is publicly available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/cpp-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261015_150115_hyperloglog_cardinality_estima}.
